title: North Pacific ship oxygen loss has no clear common AOU slope after region control on sigma0 26.5 in 2009-2021
abstract: We tested whether North Pacific ship data show less oxygen loss in high-AOU water within regions on sigma0 26.5. We reproduced the prior GLODAPv2.2023 result from the raw file. We then used cruise-region-AOU-bin means and resampled whole cruises. For 2009-2021 against 1984-1996 at a 200 km reference radius, the pooled slope above AOU 100 was +0.049 (95% interval -0.046 to +0.193). After region control it was -0.015 (-0.189 to +0.133). The transition zone and eastern gyre had no matched later casts at AOU 140 or above. The low-to-high AOU prediction therefore crossed regions. A shared oxygen reference enters both axes with the same sign, so its error can add positive covariance. Disjoint early-cruise reference tests gave uncertain slopes and lost much spatial support. They did not resolve a common positive slope within regions. This result limits use of the pooled AOU shape to locate the oxygen loss at a ventilated source. It does not make a uniform proportional oxygen-use law fit, test the float slope directly, or identify the cause of the California loss. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a static figure are included.

display.caption: Ship oxygen changes on sigma0 26.5: regional AOU bins, whole-cruise intervals, and disjoint early-cruise reference sensitivity. Split spread is not a confidence interval.
